items.title: The Record as a Condition of Review: Verbatim Reporting, Due Process, and Appellate Accountability in Oklahoma Courts
items.summary: The Record as a Condition of Review: Verbatim Reporting, Due Process, and Appellate Accountability in Oklahoma Courts A Juridical Analysis of 20 O.S. § 106.4, Oklahoma Appellate Doctrine, Electronic Recording, and the Limits of Narrative Reconstruction Current through August 25, 2026 Abstract An appellate court ordinarily reviews what the record demonstrates, not what a litigant later asserts occurred in the courtroom. That elementary principle gives court reporting a constitutional dimension that extends beyond administrative convenience. When judicial rulings, objections, argument, testimony, evidentiary exclusions, or findings are not preserved, an appellate court may be unable to determine whether error occurred. Oklahoma law addresses that danger unusually explicitly. Title 20, section 106.4 of the Oklahoma Statutes provides for full reporting of judicial proceedings by an assigned court reporter and declares that certain refusals to permit or require statements to be reported or transcribed constitute a denial of due process. items.summary: Jazz Guitar • Voice Leading • Fats Waller • Harmonic Analysis How Fats Waller’s harmonic architecture translates to the fretboard through chromatic barre-chord slides, pedal tones, walking bass, altered dominants, and economical voice leading. Ain’t Misbehavin’ does not need to be reharmonized to become harmonically fascinating. Much of that sophistication is already embedded in the song. The diminished movement, secondary dominants, relative-minor excursions, and circle-of-fifths turnaround belong to the underlying architecture. What changes on guitar is how that architecture moves . Written in 1927, the composition moved from Tin Pan Alley into swing and jazz, then eventually into Jerry Garcia’s repertoire, where its harmony became fertile ground for lyrical guitar improvisation. For a guitarist, the Garcia-influenced version is especially revealing. The song contains a descending D-minor line cliché, a sudden opening into F major, the haunting borrowed-minor movement Bb → Bbm → F , a chain of dominant sevenths, and a final section that repeatedly circles the dominant before resolving home. The central lesson of Russian Lullaby: The chords may have names, but the deeper structure is often a collection of individual voices moving by half-step. 1. items.summary: Caravan in D Minor A Jazz Manouche Guitarist’s Guide to the A7–Bb7 Vamp, Dominant Chains, Diminished Harmony, and Chromatic Improvisation For guitarists, one of the most compelling ways to approach Duke Ellington and Juan Tizol’s Caravan is the D-minor Jazz Manouche treatment. Rather than simply holding a dominant chord until the melody finally reaches the tonic, this arrangement turns the dominant itself into a rhythmic and chromatic event. The central sound is an A7 dominant pedal , repeatedly disturbed by a chord or upper structure one semitone higher, Bb7 , before the accumulated tension finally collapses into Dm . Then the bridge begins moving: D7 → G7 → C7 → F7 In the version studied here, that dominant chain continues through an especially effective chromatic turn: F7 → E7 → A7 → Dm The result is a nearly perfect laboratory for a guitarist interested in dominant harmony, diminished chords, chromatic side-slipping, arpeggio-based improvisation, and the idea that tension becomes meaningful when its destination is clear. items.summary: Shady Grove From Appalachian Modal Song to Doc Watson, Jerry Garcia, and David Grisman Some songs invite harmonic sophistication by containing many chords. Shady Grove does almost the opposite. Its extraordinary power comes from how much melody, rhythm, ambiguity, and improvisation can grow from very little harmony. At its most elemental, the tune can live almost entirely between: Dm ↔ C Two chords. Yet within that small field we can hear Appalachian old-time music, modal fiddle language, flatpicked guitar, bluegrass vocabulary, blues inflection, Garcia's spacious melodic improvisation, and David Grisman's highly conversational acoustic approach. items.title: Minor Swing: A Guitarist’s Harmonic Map to Django Reinhardt’s Masterpiece
items.summary: Minor Swing , 1937 A Guitarist’s Harmonic Map to Django Reinhardt’s Masterpiece Django Reinhardt and Stéphane Grappelli’s Minor Swing is one of those rare compositions whose apparent simplicity conceals an enormous harmonic world. The underlying form is only sixteen bars long. Its principal harmony revolves around A minor, D minor, and E7. Yet those few chords support chromaticism, diminished harmony, minor-sixth colors, tritone substitution, altered dominant sounds, and virtually the entire twelve-note chromatic vocabulary when handled with convincing voice leading. That is the central lesson of Minor Swing : improvisation is not primarily a question of finding a scale containing only “correct” notes. It is a question of knowing where the harmony is going . items.title: Accountability Without Capacity: Public Records in Crisis
items.summary: Public transparency depends on frontline employees who must process records requests, protect confidential information, answer media inquiries, and navigate complex disclosure laws. Yet many government agencies assign this legally sensitive work to undertrained and overextended general staff, creating delays, over-redaction, burnout, and declining public trust. Accountability Without Capacity: Why Transparency Systems Break at the Front Line Freedom-of-information administration is frequently treated as clerical work when it is actually a hybrid of legal analysis, records management, digital forensics, privacy protection, project management, and public communication. The resulting failures are therefore better understood as organizational-design failures than as individual incompetence. The scale of the work is substantial. Federal agencies received approximately 1.71 million FOIA requests in fiscal year 2025 and processed approximately 1.64 million. Government-wide FOIA administration used about 4,823 full-time-equivalent staff and cost an estimated $661 million, including roughly $51 million associated with litigation. items.title: Full Send Sewer and Drainage
items.summary: SPONSORED BUSINESS FEATURE When Trouble Runs Underground, Full Send Goes All In Missouri Father-and-Sons Sewer Company Brings Professional Drain, Plumbing, and Underground Utility Services Across the Four-State Region A slow drain may begin as a minor inconvenience. A backed-up sewer, broken water service, or collapsed underground line can quickly become something far more serious. When water begins rising instead of draining, unpleasant odors enter the home, or wastewater appears where it should never be, property owners need more than a temporary patch.
